item.subject: Mathematics
item.stem: Which rectangle is NOT divided into 4 equal parts?

options.label: A
options.text: [Image: Rectangle divided into 4 equal smaller rectangles]

options.label: B
options.text: [Image: Rectangle divided into 4 equal triangles]

options.label: C
options.text: [Image: Rectangle divided into 4 equal horizontal strips]

options.label: D
options.text: [Image: Rectangle divided by three parallel diagonal lines]

item.figure_description:
Four rectangular figures labeled A, B, C, and D, each partitioned into 4 regions:
- Option A: Divided into 4 equal quadrants by a vertical line and a horizontal line through the center.
- Option B: Divided into two squares by a central vertical line, with each square bisected by a diagonal from bottom-left to top-right, creating 4 identical right-angled triangles.
- Option C: Divided into 4 equal horizontal bands by three evenly spaced horizontal lines.
- Option D: Divided into 4 unequal regions by three parallel diagonal lines sloping up and to the right, creating two corner triangles and two trapezoids of unequal sizes.

reference_items.figure_description:
Five identical squares, labeled A through E, each partitioned and shaded differently:
- Option A: The square is divided horizontally into 5 equal strips. The top 2 strips are shaded grey and the bottom 3 strips are unshaded (white).
- Option B: The square is divided by a diagonal from the bottom-left corner to the top-right corner, and a line segment from the center to the bottom-right corner. The entire upper-left triangular half is shaded grey, the right triangular section is shaded grey, and the bottom triangular section is unshaded.
- Option C: The square is divided by two vertical lines into three strips: a narrow shaded strip on the left, a wide unshaded strip in the middle, and a narrow shaded strip on the right.
- Option D: An unshaded triangle has its base along the entire bottom edge of the square and its apex at the midpoint of the top edge. The two right triangles flanking it on the left and right are shaded grey.
- Option E: The square is divided by two vertical lines into 3 equal-width vertical strips. The left strip and the right strip are shaded grey, and the middle strip is unshaded.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
Jill had a rectangular piece of paper.

[Image: A rectangle divided horizontally into two equal halves by a dotted line]

She cut her paper along the dotted line and made an L shape like this.

[Image: An L-shaped figure made of two rectangular strips]

Which of these statements is true?

options.label: A
options.text: The area of the L shape is greater than the area of the rectangle.

options.label: B
options.text: The area of the L shape is equal to the area of the rectangle.

options.label: C
options.text: The area of the L shape is less than the area of the rectangle.

options.label: D
options.text: You cannot work out which area is greater without measuring.

reference_items.figure_description:
The first figure shows a horizontal rectangle with a dashed horizontal line dividing it into two equal top and bottom halves.

The second figure shows an L shape made from the two halves: one vertical rectangular strip on the left and one horizontal rectangular strip at the bottom right, joined along part of their edges at a right angle.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 2003 data, 2007 bridging data, and 2007 data (fourth-grade mathematics).

reference_items.figure_description:
Four rectangular figures labeled 1, 2, 3, and 4:
- Figure 1: A rectangle divided vertically into 4 equal strips; the 3 strips on the left are shaded gray, and the 1 strip on the right is unshaded white.
- Figure 2: A rectangle divided into a grid of 2 rows and 4 columns (8 equal parts); the 2 parts in the first column on the left are unshaded white, and the 6 parts in the other 3 columns are shaded gray.
- Figure 3: A rectangle divided vertically into 3 equal strips; the 2 strips on the left are shaded gray, and the 1 strip on the right is unshaded white.
- Figure 4: A rectangle divided into a grid of 2 rows and 2 columns (4 equal parts); the 2 parts in the left column are unshaded white, and the 2 parts in the right column are shaded gray.

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

location.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's location (difficulty) parameter b? b is on a logit scale on which the students of the calibration average about 0; a higher b means a harder item. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.

guessing.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent calibration of the TIMSS 1995 and 2003 fourth-grade mathematics data". What is the item's guessing (lower asymptote) parameter c: the probability that a student of very low ability answers it correctly, such as by guessing among the options? Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.
